newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan postpones Afghan reconciliation mission.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan postpones Afghan reconciliation mission.

text.p: Pakistan on Wednesday postponed a trip to Afghanistan by its top diplomat amid renewed charges by Kabul that Islamabad was meddling in its civil war.

The Afghan charge d'affaires in Islamabad was summoned to the Foreign Ministry and told Thursday's planned visit by ministry secretary Najmuddin Sheikh to Kabul and some provincial capitals would be rescheduled, a ministry spokesman said.
He declined to give reasons for the change, but said the Afghan diplomat was informed of Sheikh's "desire to reschedule the visit at an early date".
Sheikh had planned to reopen Pakistan's embassy in Kabul in temporary premises replacing the building that was sacked and burned by a mob of protesters a year ago.
Sheikh was also due to hold talks with officials of President Burhanuddin Rabbani's embattled government on normalising bilateral relations.
Pakistan froze contacts with the Kabul government after the embassy was burnt in protest at alleged Pakistani backing for the rebel Taleban Islamic militia, a charge denied by Islamabad.

Taleban forces, which now control a major portion of Afghanistan, have besieged Kabul for the past year from the south and southeast and are widely expected to make a fresh attempt to capture the city, depose Rabbani and install a strict Islamic order throughout Afghanistan.

Bilateral relations improved recently when Pakistan agreed to reopen its Kabul mission and sold substantial quantities of food to the Afghan government, though Taleban's latest seizure of the eastern province of Nangarhar has prevented its delivery.
Kabul began accusing Pakistan again of backing the Taleban after the militia took Nangarhar and the adjoining province of Laghman last week.
Pakistan denied the charge, and Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that Islamabad was "very disturbed to hear the accusations".
"We were concerned because we had spent many long and arduous months building bridges to the Kabul regime and recently things had seemed to brighten up," she said.
Pakistani official sources said Kabul's charges had spoiled the atmosphere and Sheikh's visit would have retarded rather than advanced the process of normalisation.

The spokesman said Pakistan continued to study recent Afghan developments, including the Taleban's efforts to consolidate its control in eastern Afghanistan, Kabul's efforts to forge an alliance with the powerful northern warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum and reports that deposed Afghan king Zahir Shah wanted to return home after 23 years of exile in Rome.
Bhutto urged warring Afghan factions on Tuesday to stop fighting and talk.
Pakistan says it has no favourites among the Afghan factions, most of whom it helped during their guerrilla war against Soviet occupation of their country in the 1980s.
